title: AlphaFold 3: Unified Atomic Modeling of All Biomolecular Complexes
whyItMatters: Extends atomic-precision structure prediction beyond isolated proteins to joint complexes of proteins, DNA, RNA, small-molecule drugs, and ions.
summary: Published in Nature by Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs, AlphaFold 3 replaced AlphaFold 2's Evoformer/structure module with a Pairformer and diffusion-based architecture capable of jointly predicting 3D structures of virtually all molecules of life. It achieved ~50% higher accuracy than prior physics-based docking tools on protein–ligand interactions and transformed everyday structural biology and drug design workflows.
technicalHighlights: Unified diffusion architecture predicts joint atomic coordinates across proteins, nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, ions, and post-translational modifications.
Substantially outperforms specialized docking tools and AlphaFold-Multimer on antibody–antigen and protein–ligand complexes.
Cited >17,000 times within two years and serves as the structural validation backbone for generative biology platforms like Evo 2.
caveats: Can hallucinate plausible-looking structures in disordered regions and predicts static snapshots rather than full conformational dynamics; initial restricted code release drew community pushback before academic weights were opened.

scoreRationale.foundational: Generalizes deep learning structural prediction from single-chain folding to the full interactome of cellular chemistry.
scoreRationale.ripple: Adopted globally across academia and pharma; directly accelerates target discovery, binder design, and genome validation.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Nature, independently benchmarked across thousands of crystal structures, and replicated by open models (Boltz, Chai, Protenix).
scoreRationale.velocity: Collapsed wet-lab structural co-crystallization cycles from months into minutes on standard hardware.
